jess_support: Customer reports 400 on /v1/rerank - response: "invalid type for 'candidates' (expected array)". Pasting minimal request/response below.

jess_support: ```
POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer sk-***

{
  "queries": ["which product is best for small teams"],
  "candidates": "[{\"id\":\"a\",\"text\":\"Product A\"},{\"id\":\"b\",\"text\":\"Product B\"}]"
}
```

jess_support: Server returned 400, body: `{"error":"invalid type for 'candidates' (expected array)"}`. Customer says they didn't intentionally stringify.

santiago_dev: Looks like candidates is a string (note the outer quotes). Most likely double-JSON-encoded on client side. Can you get a raw capture or sample client code?

jess_support: Customer pasted their Node snippet: 
```js
const candidates = [{id: 'a', text: 'Product A'}, {id: 'b', text: 'Product B'}];
const body = JSON.stringify({ queries: [q], candidates: JSON.stringify(candidates) }); // oops
await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body });
```

jess_support: They used JSON.stringify on the inner array by mistake. Repro locally with same snippet -> 400.

tim_api: Also check if any middleware is re-stringifying body (older axios usage or custom interceptors). If Content-Type was application/x-www-form-urlencoded it can get mangled. But here header is correct.

riley_se: Which SDK version? We shipped a fix in sdk-js v2.4.0 to prevent accidental double-stringify in our helper wrappers.

jess_support: Customer using sdk-js 2.3.1.

riley_se: Known failure mode: if callers pass a pre-serialized field to the v2.3 helper it won't validate types and will forward as-is. Two remediation paths:
- Quick: instruct customer to stop JSON.stringify-ing candidates and send the array directly (example below).
- Medium: upgrade to sdk-js 2.4.0 which adds a guard and clearer error text.

riley_se: Correct payload example (curl):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"queries":["which product is best for small teams"],"candidates":[{"id":"a","text":"Product A"},{"id":"b","text":"Product B"}]}'
```

jess_support: I sent the quick fix to the customer and they confirmed it succeeds. They also agreed to upgrade the SDK next week.

support-bot: Ticket #CS-8942 opened and assigned to eng oncall (riley_se) for visibility. :white_check_mark:

santiago_dev: Should we add a short note in known-issues about double-stringifying candidate lists? might save future tickets.

riley_se: Good idea — I'll file a small docs PR to the rerank examples and add explicit type check in the next patch if time.

jess_support: Closing loop with customer. Marking this thread resolved unless they hit more errors. :thumbsup:
